description: A creative software challenge where teams build quircky, unusual, and wildly entertaining software rather than traditional corporate utilities. Inspired by playful internet experiments, meme-driven mini-games, and delightful digital absurdity, participants combine unconventional UX with creative engineering to build prototypes that amuse and captivate fellow builders. Designed purely for fun and entertainment rather than high-pressure competition, this event prioritizes joy and creativity over conventional hackathon metrics. Rules: Teams must consist of 2 to 3 members (minimum 2, maximum 3). Software must focus on entertainment, absurdity, and creative UI/humor rather than enterprise utilities, system scalability, or production-grade architecture. All core logic must be authored within the official Round 2 hack window; open-source libraries, frameworks, and APIs may be used, but pre-built projects or forked templates are strictly prohibited. Teams are encouraged to build iteratively with frequent, small commits throughout the sprint. Round-wise LLM Policy: Prelims (Round 1): The use of Large Language Models (LLMs) is strictly discouraged. Round 2: Given the fast-paced 2-hour build window, the use of LLMs is welcomed and credited with no penalties. Any tech stack is allowed: Web, Mobile, CLI, IoT, Browser Extensions, or Game Engines. Registration is compulsory exclusively on Unstop and free of cost . Format: Prelims (Round 1): Online Dev Qualifier (MCQ Assessment) Held on 11th December 2026 within a flexible 3-hour window (7:00 PM – 10:00 PM IST). 30-minute online assessment taken in one continuous sitting, with strictly one attempt per team from the team leader's account (+4 for correct answers, -1 for incorrect answers). Qualifying teams advance to Round 2. Round 2: Non-Stop Rapid Prototyping Sprint & Showcase Held on 19th December 2026 (2:30 PM – 5:00 PM IST) at SMCC Building, Jadavpur University, Salt Lake Campus. Secret thematic creative constraints are revealed

raw.details:
A creative software challenge where teams build quircky, unusual, and wildly entertaining software rather than traditional corporate utilities. Inspired by playful internet experiments, meme-driven mini-games, and delightful digital absurdity, participants combine unconventional UX with creative engineering to build prototypes that amuse and captivate fellow builders. Designed purely for fun and entertainment rather than high-pressure competition, this event prioritizes joy and creativity over conventional hackathon metrics.

Rules:

  • Teams must consist of 2 to 3 members (minimum 2, maximum 3).

  • Software must focus on entertainment, absurdity, and creative UI/humor rather than enterprise utilities, system scalability, or production-grade architecture.

  • All core logic must be authored within the official Round 2 hack window; open-source libraries, frameworks, and APIs may be used, but pre-built projects or forked templates are strictly prohibited. Teams are encouraged to build iteratively with frequent, small commits throughout the sprint.

  • Round-wise LLM Policy:

    • Prelims (Round 1): The use of Large Language Models (LLMs) is strictly discouraged.

    • Round 2: Given the fast-paced 2-hour build window, the use of LLMs is welcomed and credited with no penalties.

  • Any tech stack is allowed: Web, Mobile, CLI, IoT, Browser Extensions, or Game Engines.

  • Registration is compulsory exclusively on Unstop and free of cost.

Format:

  • Prelims (Round 1): Online Dev Qualifier (MCQ Assessment)

    • Held on 11th December 2026 within a flexible 3-hour window (7:00 PM – 10:00 PM IST).

    • 30-minute online assessment taken in one continuous sitting, with strictly one attempt per team from the team leader's account (+4 for correct answers, -1 for incorrect answers).

    • Qualifying teams advance to Round 2.

  • Round 2: Non-Stop Rapid Prototyping Sprint & Showcase

    • Held on 19th December 2026 (2:30 PM – 5:00 PM IST) at SMCC Building, Jadavpur University, Salt Lake Campus.

    • Secret thematic creative constraints are revealed at the opening bell.

    • Teams build their working quirky software from scratch during the official 2.5 hour hack window and submit a short demo video and public GitHub repository.

    • All finalists receive participation certificates, and winners (Prize Pool: ₹6,000 — Winner: ₹3,000, 1st Runner-Up: ₹2,000, 2nd Runner-Up: ₹1,000) will be declared the following day.
